# FLOW-009 — Export, restore, and erase local data

Linked requirements: REQ-009  
Linked screens: SCREEN-001, SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-011, SCREEN-014

## Goal

Give the user a complete, understandable, and local-first way to move or erase their SproutPace data.

## Entry and exit conditions

Enter from Data in SCREEN-011. Exit after a successful export, a confirmed replacement restore, an exported CSV history, or a confirmed reset.

## Ordered steps

1. Choose backup, restore, CSV export, or delete all data.
2. Use the system document picker for the destination or source file.
3. Preview any replacement restore or irreversible reset before confirmation.
4. Apply the operation atomically and report a durable, actionable result.

## Branches and resume

Cancelling a picker or confirmation changes nothing. Invalid archives and failed writes preserve all existing data. A restored empty setup resumes at SCREEN-001; otherwise resume at SCREEN-002 or SCREEN-003.

## AC-090

Given product data or observation photos exist on SCREEN-002 or SCREEN-003
When the user creates a full backup from SCREEN-014 and selects a destination
Then one versioned archive containing all local product data and referenced photos is written without changing the live database.

## AC-091

Given the user selects a readable SproutPace archive on SCREEN-014
When archive validation finishes
Then SCREEN-014 shows its format version, creation time, counts, photo availability, and replacement effect before enabling confirmation.

## AC-092

Given a valid restore preview is visible on SCREEN-014
When the user confirms replacement restore
Then current product data and photos are atomically replaced, restored data is readable on SCREEN-002 and SCREEN-003, and only future reminders are rebuilt without duplicates.

## AC-093

Given a selected restore file is corrupt, unsupported, incomplete, or cannot be read
When SCREEN-014 validates or applies it
Then the operation fails with an actionable localized error and the existing database, photos, and reminders remain unchanged.

## AC-094

Given history records exist on SCREEN-003
When the user exports history as CSV from SCREEN-014
Then a UTF-8 localized-header CSV containing batch history and optional actual mass, but no photo binaries, is written to the chosen destination.

## AC-095

Given local product data, photos, or scheduled notifications exist
When the user confirms Delete all data from SCREEN-011 or SCREEN-014
Then product data, app-owned photos, and scheduled notifications are removed, previously sent Crashlytics reports are unaffected, and the app returns to SCREEN-001.

# FLOW-010 — Determine ad eligibility and manage protected-region consent

Linked requirements: REQ-010  
Linked screens: SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-007, SCREEN-011, SCREEN-015

## Goal

Monetize only eligible browsing contexts while failing closed on privacy uncertainty and never interrupting core growing work.

## Entry and exit conditions

Enter when an eligible Android catalog/history surface is opened or when the user manages applicable consent. Exit with a visible inline ad, a fully collapsed slot, or a recorded consent choice.

## Ordered steps

1. Read cached eligibility and policy metadata.
2. Refresh the fixed privacy-region endpoint when data is absent or stale.
3. If the response requires consent, collect an app-owned accept/decline choice on SCREEN-015.
4. Load at most one inline Yandex ad in the approved position; otherwise collapse the slot.

## Branches and resume

Offline, timeout, malformed response, stale policy, no fill, missing ad ID, SDK failure, or iOS no-ID all resolve to no ad. Core content remains usable.

## AC-100

Given fresh eligibility allows advertising, applicable consent is satisfied, Android has a configured Yandex ad ID, and enough content exists
When SCREEN-007 displays its fifth catalog position or SCREEN-003 History displays its sixth record position
Then one clearly labeled inline ad may appear after the fourth culture card or fifth history record, with at most one ad per eligible screen visit.

## AC-101

Given eligibility is unknown or false, consent is unresolved or declined where required, the device is offline, content is short, no fill occurs, an ID is absent, or an SDK error occurs
When SCREEN-007 or SCREEN-003 is rendered, or SCREEN-002 or SCREEN-005 is opened
Then the ad slot is fully collapsed and no ad appears on prohibited task, detail, editor, decision, settings, backup, permission, onboarding, or privacy surfaces.

## AC-102

Given a fresh endpoint response says protected-region consent is required and no valid choice exists
When the user first reaches an ad-eligible moment
Then SCREEN-015 presents clear Accept, Decline, and Privacy policy actions before any ad request is made.

## AC-103

Given stored privacy metadata exists
When advertising eligibility is evaluated for SCREEN-003 or SCREEN-007
Then the app uses it only while endpoint, policy version, region applicability, and freshness still match the contract.

## AC-104

Given fresh applicability still requires consent and the user previously accepted
When the user withdraws consent from SCREEN-011 or SCREEN-015
Then the choice is updated locally, future ad requests stop, and currently owned ad UI is removed without affecting product data.

## AC-105

Given stored consent references an older policy version
When a fresh endpoint response reports a changed policy version
Then prior consent is treated as unresolved, no ad request occurs, and SCREEN-015 is required again at the next eligible moment.

## AC-106

Given the fixed privacy-region endpoint times out, is unreachable, returns malformed data, or cannot be verified according to its response contract
When eligibility is checked
Then the app fails closed with no global consent guess, no ad request, and no interruption to SCREEN-003 or SCREEN-007 content.

## AC-107

Given the iOS build contains no Yandex ad project or ad-unit identifier
When SCREEN-003 or SCREEN-007 is rendered on iOS
Then advertising remains safely disabled and no placeholder, error, or blocked interaction is shown.

# FLOW-011 — Configure privacy-conscious crash reporting

Linked requirements: REQ-011  
Linked screens: SCREEN-011

## Goal

Collect release crash diagnostics by default while giving the user a durable, immediate opt-out and minimizing collected context.

## Entry and exit conditions

Enter during release startup or from Privacy in SCREEN-011. Exit after applying and persisting the effective Crashlytics collection preference.

## Ordered steps

1. Resolve the stored preference, defaulting to enabled only for release builds.
2. Apply the preference before routine reporting can continue.
3. Let the user disable or re-enable collection from Settings.
4. Keep debug, preview, screenshot-test, and unit-test processes disabled.

## Branches and resume

Missing platform configuration fails without blocking app startup. The visible preference reflects the effective state rather than claiming collection is active when initialization failed.

## AC-110

Given a correctly configured Android or iOS release build starts for the first time
When crash-reporting preference is resolved
Then Crashlytics automatic collection is enabled by default without enabling Analytics, user identifiers, breadcrumbs, or product-content attachments.

## AC-111

Given the user previously selected a Crashlytics collection preference on SCREEN-011
When a later release process starts
Then that stored choice is restored and applied before routine collection continues.

## AC-112

Given the Crashlytics control is visible on SCREEN-011
When the user disables or re-enables it
Then the effective collection state changes immediately where supported, the choice persists, and explanatory copy distinguishes future collection from already transmitted reports.

## AC-113

Given the app runs as debug, preview, screenshot test, or unit/integration test
When Crashlytics initialization is evaluated
Then collection stays disabled and no user ID, note, observation, culture content, ad identifier, or navigation breadcrumb is added in any build.

# FLOW-012 — Use the app across locale, theme, size, and connectivity states

Linked requirements: REQ-012  
Linked screens: SCREEN-001, SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-006, SCREEN-007, SCREEN-011

## Goal

Keep every core workflow understandable and usable in EN/RU, light/dark/system themes, supported window sizes, assistive technology, and offline conditions.

## Entry and exit conditions

Enter whenever configuration, window size, accessibility scale, or connectivity changes. Exit when the current screen has re-rendered without losing in-progress product state.

## Ordered steps

1. Resolve locale and theme preference.
2. Select compact, medium, expanded, large, or extra-large adaptive structure.
3. Reflow text and controls while preserving focus, semantics, and destination.
4. Keep local product actions available regardless of network state.

## Branches and resume

Unsupported system locales fall back to English. Network-only secondary surfaces such as ads disappear offline; local data and bundled catalog remain authoritative.

## AC-120

Given the device locale is English, Russian, or another supported system locale
When SCREEN-001, SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-006, SCREEN-007, or SCREEN-011 is opened
Then production EN or RU resources are used consistently, unsupported locales fall back to EN, and no user-authored text is translated.

## AC-121

Given theme preference is System, Light, or Dark on SCREEN-011
When system appearance changes or the user selects a preference
Then all listed core screens re-render with semantic Material roles, readable contrast, and the chosen preference persists.

## AC-122

Given font scale reaches 200%, a screen reader or keyboard is used, or the window crosses an adaptive breakpoint
When the user navigates and operates SCREEN-001, SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-006, SCREEN-007, or SCREEN-011
Then content reflows without clipping critical text/actions, focus and reading order remain logical, touch targets remain at least 48dp, and one safe-area owner consumes insets once.

## AC-123

Given the device has no network connection
When the user opens SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-006, or SCREEN-007 and performs a local core action
Then bundled catalog, plans, batches, observations, history, and settings remain usable while network-only ad content is absent.

# SCREEN-001 — First run

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-009, FLOW-012  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-009, REQ-012

## Purpose and hierarchy

Explain the promise, then offer a short optional setup for locale-aware notification time, one light zone, optional dark zone, and first tray preset. The primary action is `Continue`; `Browse catalog` skips setup without blocking later configuration.

## States

- Content: welcome, optional setup steps, and completion summary.
- Validation: inline capacity/dimension errors retain entered values.
- Permission denied: notification explanation offers retry/settings but permits completion.
- Loading, remote error, and offline: not applicable; all setup content is bundled/local.

## Actions and iconography

Use labeled buttons for Continue, Back, Skip setup, and Browse catalog. Use ASSET-001 as decorative brand art and standard arrow/notification icons only where accompanied by localized labels. Back never discards a completed prior step.

## Text layout expectations

The EN/RU promise may wrap to three lines. At 200% scale the step title, explanation, and actions stack vertically; no fixed-height copy containers. System date/time formats apply.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact uses one step per page; expanded uses a supporting preview pane without adding steps. The scaffold owns safe areas. Step progress has text semantics, focus moves to the new heading, and every target is at least 48dp.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

ASSET-001; standard navigation and notification icons declared in `app-spec.json`.

## Preview and golden matrix

EN compact welcome light/dark; RU 200% setup; notification denied; invalid dimensions; expanded completion; setup-skipped path.

# SCREEN-002 — Today

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-002, FLOW-003, FLOW-009, FLOW-010, FLOW-012  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012

## Purpose and hierarchy

Make the most important real-world action unmistakable: hero next action, overdue work, due today, then upcoming sow/harvest suggestion and capacity warning. When no work exists, show a calm next-step empty state.

## States

- Content: grouped action feed with due state and batch/culture context.
- Empty: ASSET-021 plus New batch or Browse catalog.
- Conflict: capacity warning with Resolve action.
- Permission denied: in-app work stays visible; notification recovery is secondary.
- Offline: identical local content; ads are never present.
- Loading/error: only for actual local persistence work, with retry and preserved last stable state.

## Actions and iconography

Primary row action opens or completes the due item; New batch uses labeled extended FAB when valid. Settings is the top-app-bar action. Standard today, overdue, add, settings, and warning icons supplement—not replace—text.

## Text layout expectations

Action verb and culture/tray name remain visible before secondary dates. Overdue and due-today wording is localized as complete phrases. Long names wrap to two lines; at 200% cards grow vertically.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact is a single feed. Expanded keeps one readable action column with optional capacity pane, not a stretched grid. Scaffold owns bars/insets. Headings define group order; completion and reschedule changes are announced.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

ASSET-021 and standard today, warning, add, settings, stage-action icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

EN compact mixed due work light/dark; RU 200%; all-clear empty; overdue; capacity conflict; notification denied; offline; long user batch name; expanded supporting pane.

# SCREEN-003 — Trays

Linked flows: FLOW-002, FLOW-003, FLOW-004, FLOW-007, FLOW-008, FLOW-009, FLOW-010, FLOW-012  
Linked requirements: REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012

## Purpose and hierarchy

Browse Planned, Active, and History peer categories, see status and next action, and open or create a batch. Tabs change category without implying a sequence.

## States

- Content: category list with selected detail on expanded widths.
- Empty: category-specific explanation and one useful action.
- Loading/error: local query progress/failure only; retry preserves selected tab.
- Offline: full list/detail access; History ad collapses.
- Ad state: eligible History inserts one inline item only after five real records.

## Actions and iconography

New batch is a labeled FAB where capacity does not forbid planning. Rows open detail; overflow exposes Edit, Repeat where terminal, and Delete. Use standard tray, history, add, edit, repeat, delete, and status icons with labels/semantics.

## Text layout expectations

Culture or user batch name is primary; next action/outcome and date are secondary. Tabs use localized short nouns. Long names wrap; metadata may ellipsize only after its useful prefix. Ad label is explicit in EN/RU.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact navigates list to detail; expanded uses list-detail with persistent selection. Tabs remain reachable by keyboard without requiring swipe. Selected tab, batch stage, and outcome have non-color cues. Scaffold consumes insets once.

## Allowed ad slots

History only: one labeled inline Yandex ad after the fifth real history record, only when all eligibility conditions pass. No reserved gap when hidden.

## Asset requirements

Standard tray, history, add, overflow, edit, repeat, delete, warning, and status icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Planned/Active/History content in light/dark; each empty state; RU 200%; long names; expanded list-detail; offline hidden-ad; eligible six-record History with ad; failed/abandoned outcomes.

# SCREEN-004 — Batch editor

Linked flows: FLOW-002, FLOW-004, FLOW-005, FLOW-008  
Linked requirements: REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-008

## Purpose and hierarchy

Create, edit, or repeat a planned batch from a recipe snapshot, tray preset, substrate, planned sow date, and optional fixed dates. Show capacity impact before save.

## States

- Create/edit/repeat content with locally loaded choices.
- Validation: missing recipe, invalid dates, deleted preset, and capacity conflict are inline and actionable.
- Conflict: permit changing date/zone/capacity or saving `needs_resolution` where allowed.
- Loading/error: local save only; inputs remain recoverable.
- Offline: fully available.

## Actions and iconography

Save/Confirm is the sole highest-priority action; Cancel/Back requires discard confirmation only for unsaved changes. Recipe, tray, zone, substrate, date, and conflict selectors use standard labeled Material controls and icons.

## Text layout expectations

Units are explicit (`cm`); dates use locale conventions. Fixed-date explanation is a complete sentence. At 200% labels remain associated with inputs and trailing icons move rather than overlap text.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact is a scrolling form with a safe bottom action area; expanded adds a plan summary pane. Error focus moves to the first invalid field; date and selection controls support keyboard/manual alternatives. One scaffold owns insets.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard save, date, tray, zone, substrate, warning, and navigation icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Create light/dark; edit; repeat; RU 200%; invalid dimensions/date; capacity conflict; needs-resolution save; long recipe name; expanded summary.

# SCREEN-005 — Batch detail

Linked flows: FLOW-002, FLOW-003, FLOW-004, FLOW-007, FLOW-008, FLOW-010, FLOW-012  
Linked requirements: REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-010, REQ-012

## Purpose and hierarchy

Explain current reality through next action, stage timeline, capacity assignment, recipe snapshot, observations, and history. Actual events and predicted windows must be visually distinct.

## States

- Planned, active, ready, harvested, failed, and abandoned content.
- Skipped stage and fixed-date variants.
- Actual overflow with Temporarily unassigned resolution.
- Empty observations with Add observation.
- Local loading/error and full offline operation.

## Actions and iconography

Primary action confirms the next actual stage or closes the batch. Secondary actions add observation, edit, skip stage, undo last transition, reassign, repeat, or delete as applicable. Use ASSET-016–020 stage art decoratively plus labeled standard action icons.

## Text layout expectations

Next action and culture name precede dates. Timeline labels distinguish Actual, Expected, Skipped, and Fixed. Notes wrap without arbitrary truncation; optional mass always displays its metric unit.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact stacks summary, timeline, and observations. Expanded uses a supporting detail pane but preserves reading order. Timeline exposes an ordered semantic list; state never relies only on color. Keyboard focus and screen-reader announcement follow successful transitions.

## Allowed ad slots

None, including terminal history detail.

## Asset requirements

ASSET-016, ASSET-017, ASSET-018, ASSET-019, ASSET-020; standard edit, observation, photo, undo, skip, move, repeat, close, and delete icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Each lifecycle stage light/dark; ready with fixed date; skipped stage; temporary unassigned; observations with photo; terminal outcomes; RU 200%; long note; offline; expanded timeline.

/** Application-scoped production graph. Hosts construct and retain exactly one instance. */
class ProductionAppGraph internal constructor(
    driverFactory: SqlDriverFactory,
    settings: Settings,
    private val privateFileStore: PrivateFileStore,
    private val pendingPhotoImportStore: PendingPhotoImportStore,
    documentPort: ArchiveDocumentPort,
    reminderDriver: ReminderDriver,
    private val notificationPermissionService: NotificationPermissionService,
    crashReportingDriver: CrashReportingDriver,
    ioDispatcher: CoroutineDispatcher,
    mainContext: CoroutineContext,
    isDebug: Boolean,
    releaseStoreFactory: StoreFactory,
    debugStoreFactory: StoreFactory,
    lifecycleRegistry: LifecycleRegistry = LifecycleRegistry(),
    nowEpochMillis: () -> Long = { Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds() },
    timeZone: () -> TimeZone = { TimeZone.currentSystemDefault() },
) : AutoCloseable {
    private val lifecycleRegistry = lifecycleRegistry.also { it.create() }
    private val database = LocalDatabase(driverFactory, ioDispatcher)
    val productSettings: ProductSettings = MultiplatformProductSettings(settings)
    private val applicationScope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + ioDispatcher)
    private val crashReportingCoordinator = CrashReportingCoordinator(
        productSettings,
        crashReportingDriver,
        if (isDebug) RuntimeEnvironment.DEBUG else RuntimeEnvironment.RELEASE,
    )
    private val mutableCrashReportingState = MutableStateFlow(crashReportingCoordinator.applyStoredPreference())
    private val reminderPlanSource = SnapshotReminderPlanSource(
        snapshot = { database.snapshot() },
        settings = productSettings,
        nowEpochMillis = nowEpochMillis,
        timeZone = timeZone,
    )
    private val reminderCoordinator = ReminderLifecycleCoordinator(
        permissionService = notificationPermissionService,
        planSource = reminderPlanSource,
        reconciler = ReminderReconciler(reminderDriver),
        clock = EpochMillisClock(nowEpochMillis),
    )
    private val reminderPort = SnapshotReminderReconciliationPort(reminderCoordinator)
    private val workspaceRepository = LocalWorkspaceRepository(database, privateFileStore, ioDispatcher)
    private lateinit var rootComponent: AppRootComponent
    private val backupService = LocalBackupService(
        database = database,
        files = privateFileStore,
        settings = productSettings,
        ioDispatcher = ioDispatcher,
        documents = documentPort,
        reminders = reminderPort,
        output = FirstRunNavigationOutput(mainContext) { rootComponent.resetToFirstRun() },
    )
    private val productionDataManager = ProductionScreenDataManager(
        database = database,
        settings = productSettings,
        workspaceRepository = workspaceRepository,
        backupService = backupService,
        pendingPhotos = pendingPhotoImportStore,
    )
    private val screenDataManager = ReminderAwareScreenDataManager(
        delegate = CrashAwareScreenDataManager(productionDataManager, mutableCrashReportingState.asStateFlow()),
        settings = productSettings,
        permissionService = notificationPermissionService,
        reconcile = ::reconcile,
    )
    private var closed = false

    private val productionRoot: AppRootComponent = AppRootFactory(
        productionRootDependencies(
            releaseStoreFactory = releaseStoreFactory,
            debugStoreFactory = debugStoreFactory,
            isDebug = isDebug,
            screenDataManager = screenDataManager,
            mainContext = mainContext,
        ),
    ).create(DefaultComponentContext(lifecycleRegistry)).also { rootComponent = it }
    val root: AppRootComponent = ThemedAppRootComponent(productionRoot, productSettings.theme)

    val lifecycleState: Lifecycle.State get() = lifecycleRegistry.state

    init {
        applicationScope.launch { runCatching { pendingPhotoImportStore.clear() } }
        applicationScope.launch {
            productSettings.crashReportingEnabled.collect { preference ->
                mutableCrashReportingState.value = crashReportingCoordinator.applyPreference(preference)
            }
        }
        reconcile(ReconciliationReason.APP_START)
    }

    fun onStart() = lifecycleRegistry.start()
    fun onResume() {
        lifecycleRegistry.resume()
        applicationScope.launch { runCatching { reminderCoordinator.onHostResume() } }
    }
    fun onPause() = lifecycleRegistry.pause()
    fun onStop() = lifecycleRegistry.stop()

    fun requestNotificationPermission() {
        applicationScope.launch {
            runCatching {
                notificationPermissionService.request()
                reminderCoordinator.reconcile(ReconciliationReason.PERMISSION_RESTORED)
            }
        }
    }

    fun reconcile(reason: ReconciliationReason) {
        applicationScope.launch { runCatching { reminderCoordinator.reconcile(reason) } }
    }

    override fun close() {
        if (closed) return
        closed = true
        applicationScope.cancel()
        lifecycleRegistry.destroy()
        pendingPhotoImportStore.close()
        privateFileStore.close()
        database.close()
    }
}

    override val themePreference: StateFlow<com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.data.ThemePreference>,
) : AppRootComponent by delegate, ThemePreferenceOwner

internal class CrashAwareScreenDataManager(
    private val delegate: ScreenDataManager,
    private val runtimeState: StateFlow<CrashReportingState>,
) : ScreenDataManager {
    override fun watch(screen: ScreenId, stableId: String?): Flow<ScreenSnapshot> {
        val source = delegate.watch(screen, stableId)
        if (screen != ScreenId.SETTINGS) return source
        return combine(source, runtimeState) { snapshot, state ->
            snapshot.copy(
                items = snapshot.items.map { item ->
                    if (item.id == "crash-reporting") item.copy(stateKey = state.textKey()) else item
                },
                facts = snapshot.facts.filterNot { it.id == "crash-reporting-effective" } +
                    com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.ScreenFact(
                        id = "crash-reporting-effective",
                        labelKey = TextKey("settings_crash_reporting_effective"),
                        valueKey = state.textKey(),
                    ),
            )
        }
    }

    override suspend fun execute(screen: ScreenId, command: ScreenCommand): Result<ScreenSnapshot> =
        delegate.execute(screen, command)

    private fun CrashReportingState.textKey() = TextKey(when (this) {
        is CrashReportingState.Active -> "crash_reporting_active"
        is CrashReportingState.Unavailable -> "crash_reporting_unavailable"
        is CrashReportingState.Disabled -> when (reason) {
            DisableReason.USER_CHOICE -> "crash_reporting_user_off"
            DisableReason.NON_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT -> "crash_reporting_build_disabled"
        }
    })
}

internal class SnapshotReminderReconciliationPort(
    private val coordinator: ReminderLifecycleCoordinator?,
    private val legacyDriver: ReminderDriver? = null,
    private val legacyNowEpochMillis: (() -> Long)? = null,
) : ReminderReconciliationPort {
    constructor(coordinator: ReminderLifecycleCoordinator) : this(coordinator, null, null)
    constructor(driver: ReminderDriver, nowEpochMillis: () -> Long) : this(null, driver, nowEpochMillis)

    override suspend fun replaceFutureReminders(snapshot: ProductSnapshot) {
        coordinator?.onRestoreCompleted() ?: run {
            val driver = requireNotNull(legacyDriver)
            val desired = snapshot.futureSoakReminders(requireNotNull(legacyNowEpochMillis).invoke()).associateBy { it.id }
            val existing = driver.registeredIds()
            (existing - desired.keys).sortedBy { it.value }.forEach { driver.cancel(it).getOrThrow() }
            desired.values.sortedBy { it.id.value }.forEach { driver.schedule(it).getOrThrow() }
        }
    }
}

internal class SnapshotReminderPlanSource(
    private val snapshot: suspend () -> ProductSnapshot,
    private val settings: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.data.ProductSettings,
    private val nowEpochMillis: () -> Long,
    private val timeZone: () -> TimeZone,
) : ReminderPlanSource {
    override suspend fun currentPlan(): ReminderPlan {
        val now = nowEpochMillis()
        val current = snapshot()
        val preferences = settings.snapshot()
        val dueCount = current.batches.asSequence()
            .filterNot { it.state.isTerminal }
            .flatMap { it.actions.asSequence() }
            .count { it.status == ScheduledActionStatus.PENDING && SchedulingEngine.resolvedInstant(it).toEpochMilliseconds() <= now }
        val daily = if (preferences.notificationsEnabled && dueCount > 0) {
            PhysicalReminder(
                id = PhysicalReminderId(DAILY_SUMMARY_ID),
                kind = ReminderKind.DAILY_SUMMARY,
                fireAtEpochMillis = nextSummaryAt(now, preferences.summaryTime, timeZone()),
                titleKey = NativeTextKey.DAILY_SUMMARY_TITLE,
                bodyKey = NativeTextKey.DAILY_SUMMARY_BODY,
            )
        } else null
        val soak = if (preferences.soakRemindersEnabled) current.futureSoakReminders(now) else emptyList()
        return ReminderPlan(dueCount, daily, soak)
    }

    private fun nextSummaryAt(now: Long, localTime: SummaryLocalTime, zone: TimeZone): Long {
        val nowLocal = kotlinx.datetime.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(now).toLocalDateTime(zone)
        var date = nowLocal.date
        var candidate = LocalDateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, localTime.hour, localTime.minute)
            .toInstant(zone).toEpochMilliseconds()
        if (candidate <= now) {
            date = date.plus(1, DateTimeUnit.DAY)
            candidate = LocalDateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, localTime.hour, localTime.minute)
                .toInstant(zone).toEpochMilliseconds()
        }
        return candidate
    }

    private companion object {
        const val DAILY_SUMMARY_ID = "sproutpace:daily-summary"
    }
}

internal class FirstRunNavigationOutput(
    private val mainContext: CoroutineContext,
    private val resetToFirstRun: () -> Unit,
) : LocalDataIntegrationOutput {
    override suspend fun emit(event: LocalDataIntegrationEvent) {
        if (event == LocalDataIntegrationEvent.FirstRunNavigationRequired) {
            withContext(mainContext) { resetToFirstRun() }
        }
    }
}

internal class ReminderAwareScreenDataManager(
    private val delegate: ScreenDataManager,
    private val settings: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.data.ProductSettings,
    private val permissionService: NotificationPermissionService,
    private val reconcile: (ReconciliationReason) -> Unit,
) : ScreenDataManager {
    override fun watch(screen: ScreenId, stableId: String?): Flow<ScreenSnapshot> {
        val source = delegate.watch(screen, stableId)
        if (screen != ScreenId.NOTIFICATIONS) return source
        val preferences = combine(
            settings.notificationsEnabled,
            settings.summaryTime,
            settings.soakRemindersEnabled,
        ) { daily, time, soak -> Triple(daily, time, soak) }
        return combine(source, preferences, permissionService.state) { snapshot, values, permission ->
            snapshot.copy(
                items = listOf(
                    ScreenItem("daily-summary", titleKey = TextKey("notifications_daily_summary"), stateKey = booleanKey(values.first)),
                    ScreenItem("summary-time", titleKey = TextKey("notifications_time"), authoredTitle = values.second.toString()),
                    ScreenItem("soak-reminder", titleKey = TextKey("notifications_soak_reminder"), stateKey = booleanKey(values.third)),
                ),
                permissionState = permission.toComponentPermissionState(),
            )
        }
    }

    override suspend fun execute(screen: ScreenId, command: ScreenCommand): Result<ScreenSnapshot> =
        delegate.execute(screen, command).fold(
            onSuccess = { snapshot ->
                if (command.operation in REMINDER_MUTATIONS || command.operation == "update-notifications") {
                    reconcile(ReconciliationReason.PRODUCT_DATA_CHANGED)
                }
                Result.success(snapshot)
            },
            onFailure = { Result.failure(it) },
        )

    private fun booleanKey(value: Boolean) = TextKey(if (value) "state_enabled" else "state_disabled")

    private fun PermissionState.toComponentPermissionState() = when (this) {
        PermissionState.Unknown, PermissionState.Checking, PermissionState.Requesting ->
            com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.PermissionState.NOT_REQUESTED
        PermissionState.Granted -> com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.PermissionState.GRANTED
        is PermissionState.Denied -> if (canRequestAgain) {
            com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.PermissionState.DENIED
        } else {
            com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.PermissionState.PERMANENTLY_DENIED
        }
        PermissionState.Unavailable -> com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.PermissionState.NOT_REQUIRED
    }

    private companion object {
        val REMINDER_MUTATIONS = setOf(
            "save-batch", "delete-batch", "delete-batch-cascade", "confirm-sowing", "confirm-stage",
            "undo-stage", "skip-stage", "complete-action", "snooze", "skip-action", "schedule-soak-target",
            "time-zone-change", "close-harvest", "close-failed", "close-abandoned", "save-outcome",
        )
    }
}

private fun ProductSnapshot.futureSoakReminders(nowEpochMillis: Long): List<PhysicalReminder> =
    batches.flatMap { batch ->
        batch.actions.mapNotNull { action ->
            val fireAt = SchedulingEngine.resolvedInstant(action).toEpochMilliseconds()
            if (action.status != ScheduledActionStatus.PENDING || action.stage != GrowStage.SOAKING ||
                fireAt <= nowEpochMillis
            ) {
                null
            } else {
                PhysicalReminder(
                    id = PhysicalReminderId("sproutpace:soak:${batch.id.value}:${action.id.value}"),
                    kind = ReminderKind.SOAK,
                    fireAtEpochMillis = fireAt,
                    titleKey = NativeTextKey.SOAK_COMPLETE_TITLE,
                    bodyKey = NativeTextKey.SOAK_COMPLETE_BODY,
                )
            }
        }
    }

# Production UI redesign review — 2026-09-27

Status: Accepted

Blocking findings: none

## Evidence reviewed

- Approved product behavior: `spec/app-spec.json` and `spec/screens/SCREEN-001.md` through `SCREEN-016.md`.
- Research baseline: [Lazyweb cross-screen product UI research](https://www.lazyweb.com/agentic-search/0d8da7b5-4c89-4516-99bb-ce0e2b7d76ba).
- Visual evidence: all 78 tracked Paparazzi goldens, including light, dark, expanded, error/conflict/permission states, and RU at 200% font scale.
- Runtime evidence: `.vibe/scripts/run-android-ui-smoke.ps1` on a Pixel 8 AVD at 420 dpi. It verifies the accessibility tree, 48dp targets, keyboard focus and activation, notification permission denial/recovery, Android system-settings recovery, process restart, manual time entry, save completion, and persistence after restart.
- Shared system: `SproutPaceTypography`, `SproutPaceShapes`, Material color roles, adaptive navigation, and common action/form presentation in `shared/compose`.

## Screen-by-screen closure

| Screen | Review result | Final disposition |
|---|---|---|
| SCREEN-001 — First run | Accepted | Keeps the approved setup and catalog escape route; the supporting visual is calm and no technical identifiers are exposed. |
| SCREEN-002 — Today | Accepted | One clear next action, quieter supporting state, meaningful empty state, and stable Settings access. |
| SCREEN-003 — Trays | Accepted | Planned/Active/History remain peer tabs with adaptive list-detail behavior and category-specific empty states. |
| SCREEN-004 — Batch editor | Accepted | The approved staged form remains intact; fields, capacity feedback, and primary completion action share the common form system. |
| SCREEN-005 — Batch detail | Accepted | Stage progression stays dominant; expected/actual/skipped/fixed meaning is not color-only and secondary actions are demoted. |
| SCREEN-006 — Plan | Accepted | The linear rhythm and conflict model remain legible without low-value dashboard counters or a misleading calendar metaphor. |
| SCREEN-007 — Catalog | Accepted | Search is a first-class rounded Material field; image-led cards retain provenance, offline behavior, and adaptive columns. |
| SCREEN-008 — Recipe | Accepted | Stage content and provenance remain available without generic section labels or repeated summaries. |
| SCREEN-009 — Observation | Accepted | Date, note, and private photo actions remain; storage IDs and redundant helper cards are absent. |
| SCREEN-010 — Close batch | Accepted | Outcome selection is the focus and one Save outcome action replaces redundant outcome shortcut buttons. |
| SCREEN-011 — Settings | Accepted | Quiet grouped rows, readable switch labels, and clear privacy/data consequences hold at RU 200% scale. |
| SCREEN-012 — Zones | Accepted | Capacity and conflict meaning remain visible; record IDs are hidden and destructive actions use low-emphasis error treatment. |
| SCREEN-013 — Tray sizes | Accepted | Metric dimensions and snapshot-safe consequences remain clear without record IDs or generic headings. |
| SCREEN-014 — Backup/restore | Accepted | Action-led rows avoid duplicate full-width actions; restore metadata appears only when it changes the decision. |
| SCREEN-015 — Advertising privacy | Accepted | Neutral context and equally understandable consent choices are preserved; declining remains a complete path. |
| SCREEN-016 — Notifications | Accepted | Editable switches/time are shown once, permission recovery is explicit, and device smoke proves denial, settings recovery, manual input, save, and restart persistence. |

## Cross-screen conclusions

- The common typography and shape scale are applied at the Material theme boundary; screens do not define competing type systems.
- Primary, secondary, outlined, and destructive actions now communicate hierarchy consistently.
- Generic Items/Details/Actions headings, technical IDs, duplicate Backup actions, duplicate Close batch outcomes, and repeated notification summaries were removed.
- Current goldens show no clipping or overlap in the reviewed compact, expanded, dark, and RU/200% states.
- The redesign changes presentation, not approved product scope or business rules.

## Release boundary

This review closes the product-design surface, not every external release gate. Publication is not requested in this delivery, so store publication/signing, production Firebase symbolication, production Yandex ad-device validation, and store/privacy disclosure publication are inactive until their required external projects, credentials, policy URL, and explicit publication request exist. Safe development defaults remain required by the project guide. macOS Simulator execution and `xcodebuild` remain CI/macOS-only evidence and must not be reported as locally passed on Windows.

# Production UI redesign

Status: active lean delivery goal (2026-09-27).

## Outcome

Bring every approved SproutPace screen to one production-ready Material 3 system without changing product scope. The redesign must preserve the full behavior in `spec/app-spec.json`, EN/RU resources, offline-first operation, adaptive layouts, accessibility, deterministic previews, and Android/iOS Compose Multiplatform buildability.

## Evidence and direction

- Lazyweb screen research covers onboarding, task dashboards, segmented active/history lists, multi-step forms, lifecycle/timeline detail, planning, searchable catalogs, journal/photo forms, settings, capacity, dimensions, backup/restore, privacy consent, and notification recovery.
- Reusable patterns: a single dominant task, compact contextual summaries, tabbed peer categories, quiet grouped settings, full-width form actions, explicit empty states, and equal clarity for privacy choices.
- Rejected patterns: dashboards filled with low-value counters, card-on-card nesting, generic section labels, repeated summaries, long stacks of equal-prominence outlined buttons, and controls that expose storage IDs or raw timestamps.
- Material 3 baseline components are the cross-platform fallback. The repository uses Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0 and Material3 1.12.0-alpha03; experimental expressive APIs are not required for visual parity.

## Shared design contract

- Typography: one sans-serif EN/RU-safe Material role scale; semibold headlines/titles and controls; normal-weight body copy; no screen-local font sizes.
- Shape: 6/10/14/20/28dp theme scale. Large and extra-large shapes are reserved for meaningful cards, search, hero summaries, and dialogs.
- Color: forest/lime brand roles remain semantic. Primary marks the single highest-priority action. Tertiary containers communicate warnings; error roles are reserved for errors and destructive consequences.
- Surfaces: use whitespace and tonal hierarchy before borders or elevation. Do not wrap every section in a card.
- Forms: Material fields and selection controls, 48dp targets, inline errors, retained input, visible units, locale-aware dates/times, and no exposed technical identifiers.
- Actions: one filled primary action; tonal secondary actions; destructive actions use error-colored low-emphasis treatment and explicit confirmation where required.
- Navigation: four stable destinations (Today, Trays, Plan, Catalog), bottom navigation under 600dp and rail above it. One scaffold owns safe insets.
- Accessibility: headings describe real sections; state is never color-only; dynamic errors/progress are announced; all controls remain operable at 200% text scale and by keyboard/pointer where supported.
- Motion: restrained standard Material motion; no decorative loading or interaction-delaying transitions; reduced-motion behavior remains safe.

## Screen audit

| Screen | Spec-critical hierarchy | Redesign disposition |
|---|---|---|
| First run | Promise, optional setup, Continue/Browse catalog | Keep step flow; remove generic Items/Details/Actions framing and internal IDs. |
| Today | Next action, overdue, due, suggestion/conflict | Preserve hero; keep secondary work quieter and avoid dashboard counters. |
| Trays | Planned/Active/History peers, next action | Preserve tabs; maintain category-specific empty state and list-detail adaptation. |
| Batch editor | Recipe/tray, details, capacity, review | Preserve three-step form and safe bottom primary action. |
| Batch detail | Next action, ordered stages, assignment, observations | Use meaningful Stages heading; distinguish actual/expected/skipped/fixed without color alone. |
| Plan | Harvest rhythm, confirmed/suggested queue, conflict | Preserve linear timeline; avoid a calendar metaphor and reduce equal-weight action buttons. |
| Catalog | Search, bundled/personal cards, provenance | Treat search as a first-class rounded M3 field; keep offline/ad behavior and image-led cards. |
| Recipe | Guide/editor, stages, provenance | Use Stages rather than Items; retain source/version/review metadata without duplicate summaries. |
| Observation | Date, note, optional private photo | Remove repeated helper cards and technical observation ID; keep photo actions labeled. |
| Close batch | Outcome, date, optional details, consequence | Make outcome choice the focus; remove duplicated help and keep Save outcome singular. |
| Settings | Setup, preferences, privacy/data, reset | Current grouped list is the reference pattern; keep switches from squeezing text at 200%. |
| Zones | Name/type/capacity/occupancy/conflicts | Remove generic headings and record ID; keep add/edit/delete hierarchy and consequences. |
| Tray sizes | Shape/name/metric dimensions | Remove generic headings and record ID; show units and snapshot-safe delete consequence. |
| Backup/restore | Backup, preview restore, CSV, reset | Keep action-led rows; show preview metadata only when it changes the decision. |
| Advertising privacy | Neutral context, equal Accept/Decline, policy | Remove repeated context cards; keep actions equally clear and back non-consenting. |
| Notifications | Summary/soak switches, time, permission recovery | Remove repeated summary; keep immediate switches, locale time, and Today-as-source-of-truth copy. |

## Verification contract

- Keep light/dark previews for all primary screens and risk states.
- Keep RU at 200% font scale, long-authored text, empty/error/conflict/permission states, and materially distinct expanded layouts.
- Record Paparazzi goldens only after intentional review, then run verification.
- Run affected Compose tests while iterating. At a stable snapshot run applicable lean Gradle gates, report Windows/macOS boundaries, and obtain an independent acceptance audit before claiming global completion.

## Recovery note

Current milestone: research, implementation, and current-state visual review are complete. Shared typography and shape tokens now drive the theme; the generic layout no longer exposes technical IDs or meaningless Items/Details/Actions headings; action emphasis is consistent; search has a dedicated rounded field; repeated Backup actions, Close batch outcome shortcuts, and notification summary cards were removed. The complete 78-image Paparazzi set was regenerated, with every screen family inspected across representative light, dark, expanded, and RU 200% states. The accepted review is recorded in `docs/design-review/production-ui-redesign-20260927.md`.

Verified on Windows: the full applicable lean Gradle matrix passed, including Detekt, Android host tests, Compose compilation, SQLDelight migration verification, Paparazzi verification, Android debug/release artifacts, iOS target compilation, and Kover verification. Asset validation passes. A Pixel 8 emulator smoke proves accessibility hierarchy, minimum targets, keyboard operation, permission denial/recovery, system settings recovery, manual time entry, save completion, and restart persistence. The iOS simulator and `xcodebuild` remain macOS/CI-only evidence.

Next action: refresh the stable receipts for the final source snapshot and obtain a fresh independent acceptance audit. Do not claim global release readiness without macOS/CI evidence for the remaining Apple-only gates.
